summary: Sidecar metrics lock + healthcheck flood causing API 5xx elevation and upstream runtime CPU saturation
description:
Issue summary:
During a sustained healthcheck spike from a downstream customer (NimbusAI), the api-gateway began returning a high rate of 5xx responses (502/503). Concurrently we observed CPU saturation on a subset of serving runtimes and prolonged response times from the sidecar metrics collector.

Impact:
- Customer-facing ratio of 5xx increased from baseline ~0.02% to 6.8% over a 12-minute window.
- NimbusAI (dedicated tenant) reported failed inference calls and stream drops.
- Affected traffic covered 2 AZs in us-east-1; overall platform error budget impacted briefly.

Environment:
- prod, us-east-1 region
- Dedicated pool: nvme-backed GPU nodes serving redwood-open-1 model variants

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Healthcheck flood from a misconfigured internal probe on NimbusAI side (high-frequency synthetic requests).
2) api-gateway enqueue/backpressure increased; concurrent healthchecks saturated sidecar metrics lock attempting to write metrics to local agent.
3) Sidecar thread holding metrics lock blocked the proxy's keepalive/accept path, increasing accept queue latency.
4) Serving runtime CPU increased as runtime threads waited on connection handoffs; NVML driver saw transient timeouts and a few GPU watchdog resets.
5) Gateway replies degraded to 502/503 for in-flight requests.

Observed behavior:
- p95 latency for API route /v1/generate jumped from 220ms -> 1.8s.
- 5xx rate peak: 6.8% at 09:11 UTC.
- Sidecar logs show repeated "metrics_writer: lock contention" entries and ~200ms+ blocked durations.
- Grafana panels: connection_reset_count increased by 120 within 10 minutes; nvml_gputimeout_count recorded 3 events.

Expected behavior:
- Healthchecks should be rate-limited at ingress and never cause sidecar-level lock contention or upstream runtime CPU saturation.
- Gateway should shed healthcheck-only traffic earlier to protect serving runtimes.

Logs / links:
- Grafana (alert): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/5xx-sidecar-lock-2026-03-12
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0SUPPORT/p1648
- Sidecar log excerpt: "2026-03-12T09:09:42Z metrics_writer: lock contention 245ms (queue=18)"

Initial triage notes:
- Hypothesis A: Misbehaving external probe triggered a high-rate healthcheck stream that bypassed normal rate-limiter and repeatedly polled /health on tenant route causing local sidecar to contend on a mutex used for batching metrics writes.
- Hypothesis B: Metrics writer lock held during a flush to disk/agent while the api-gateway accept queue grew, causing unbounded queueing and proxy-side request timeouts.
- Evidence: Sidecar contention log aligned exactly with p95 latency spike and increased accept queue depth in the apigw metrics.

Immediate actions taken:
- Support temporarily blocked the misbehaving source (NimbusAI probe IP) at the edge (rate-limit + IP ban) at 09:16 UTC — 5xx rate dropped to 0.6% within 3 minutes.
- Opened INT-4102 to coordinate a sidecar hotfix; deployment planned to remove blocking flush behavior.
- Added ad-hoc alert for sidecar-metrics-lock-duration > 100ms.

Workaround for affected customers:
- Rate-limited healthchecks on customer-side (instructed NimbusAI to reduce probe frequency to <1/min) and applied edge rate-limits.

Next steps / action plan:
1) Engineering (runtime & sidecar) to roll a sidecar patch that converts the metrics writer to a lock-free ring buffer (PR linked). Target hotfix window: 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
2) Add platform-level guard to drop high-frequency /health requests above 30/min per source IP and emit a dedicated healthcheck-shed metric.
3) Postmortem to document root cause and customer guidance; coordinate with NimbusAI for long-term remediation.

Customer impact note:
- NimbusAI experienced transient failed requests but did not exceed SLO credits. We informed CS and Nimbus account team; they accepted temporary mitigation and will apply configuration changes.

investigation_notes: Artifacts collected: sidecar logs, apigw accept queue histogram, nvml watchdog logs. Flamegraphs show kernel wait on futex in metrics writer thread. Reproduced in staging by running a synthetic /health flood from an IP without rate-limit — produced identical lock contention pattern. Patch changes metrics writer to async buffer + background flush. Canary shows p95 restore to baseline.
workaround: Edge-level IP rate-limit applied to offending probe; instructed customer to throttle healthchecks. Added temporary alert and monitoring dashboards to detect recurrence.
resolution: In progress — hotfix deployed to canary and scheduled for gradual rollout. Customer mitigation accepted. Postmortem pending.
